source="" altitude="448.83" datetime="" author="" heading="-112.171" description="The Seven-Mau Coconut Forest" info="7 hectare water coconut village has become a appealing ecotourism destination with vast lush palm groves sketching out to the Cửa Đại estuary. . 

It is just 3 km southeast of Hoi An ancient town, lying on a downstream area of ​​three large rivers: Thu Bon, Co Co and Truong Giang. 

    The name of this place originated from locals of Thanh Chau village who used to be famous for their boat trading business, each trading trip lasted for months. Some traders went to Southern Vietnam and brought the coconut water to plant in Cam Thanh. Seeing that the water coconut tree grows well, they officially asked the government to plant 7 acres of water coconut, from which there is the name of the 7 hectare water coconut village. In fact, Cam Thanh coconut forest has naturally grown into a forest of hundreds of hectares (according to statistics in 2017, there are 118 hectares of coconut forest, including 26 hectares of 1-year-old planted forest along Cua Dai Bridge) 

    Cam Thanh is a typical manifestation of the mangrove ecosystem in the central coastal estuary with typical ecosystems of the tropics being mangrove forests and seagrasses. It is the buffer zone of the Cu Lao Cham - Hoi An World Biosphere Reserve. The 7 hectare coconut forest has a mangrove ecosystem near the rich sea as a home to numerous valuable aquatic species, specially shrimp, crabs, fish, mollusks and some birds. This place plays as a biological purifier, which helps to regulate the climate, prevent erosion, increase sediment, improve environmental quality and maintain ecological balance. 

    With the terrain of discreet mangrove coconut forests and surrounding rivers, it is convenient for guerrilla warfare. Cam Thanh village was used as a revolutionary base for the local Vietnamese soldiers in Hoi An during two wars against the French and the American, witnessing many resounding triumphs. However, over a long period of time, most of these works no longer exist. In particular, during the anti American resistance, the 7 hectare coconut forest also became a solid base, a place to protect and preserve our armed forces to fight and defeat the enemy. On the night of September 27, 1964, the people of Cam Thanh stood up in unison. With diversionary tactics, they used coconut shells to deceive and suppress the enemy. The general uprising with the fake coconut shell guns in 7 hectares of coconut forest has become a legend of Hoian revolutionary history. 

“Stand up with a coconut shell gun. 

    Our homeland revolted, America lost, the puppet government fell.” 

The war has passed and the 7 hectare coconut forest is one of the proofs associated with the resounding feats of the Hoian army and locals in particular and the Quang Nam people in general. 

    Besides, Cam Thanh is also the convergence of some famous traditional craft villages such as:fish sauce making, bamboo and coconut painting making, swallow raising,ect. 

“Ho khoan” singing: Since the olden days, we’ve heard the melodies and songs of the local people and this is also a type of intangible cultural heritage that has been preserved and promoted through generations. In which, the art of “ bả trạo” singing is a type of coastal folk performance, a unique cultural feature of the people associated with the stormy sea. 

    The songs and dances express the attitude of respect, recreating the arduous seafaring work, reflecting the true and delicate working and spiritual life of the locals. 

Previously, Cam Thanh was a place where fishing by boats developed, so this form of performance was soon shaped and passed down. In addition, this place also preserves the simple, rustic yet profound folk songs and chants, creating a unique language that reflects the rich and diverse inner life of the people here. It was also considered as the meeting place for young men and women to communicate. 

    Take a look at the image of people throwing the cast net over there, which is also known as fishing nets. In addition to wet rice cultivation and forestry, fishing is also a unique occupation of the Vietnamese people, which has appeared and existed throughout the history of Vietnam. Activities such as boat-knocking, throwing cast nets, pulling nets, and sorting fish are the basic tasks that fishermen must do everyday. Every time the sun sets, people have to get on the boat and go out to sea, and when the sun rises, people return to shore. The rewards that people receive from the sea are all kinds of different seafood products such as: shrimp, crab, fish, squid, ect. 

    Fishing is a job drifting on the river that requires most of the young men who are the breadwinners of the family to participate. The image of the people and the boat has entered poetry and folk songs that are imbued with the homeland and they have been preserved and passed down to this day. 

   Next, we’ll enjoy one more type of basket boat dance, a unique art form that only exists in the Cam Thanh river region. 

"The basket boat sways hesitantly carrying me across the pond. The basket boat tilted. 

The basket boat wobbled. 

A pair of rowing chopsticks, a piece of fishing net. 

The drops of water that splashed up wet my peachy cheeks.” 

    The basket boat is not only a livelihood of the people but also an item that hides many memories. It witnesses many ups and downs and becomes an indispensable image in festivals. Basket boat dancing is one of the most interesting experiences that if you miss it, you may lose a part of sightseeing on this trip. " comment="<b style="font-size: 17px"
